description: Skyline as a mod: tool.call hooks on Read, Grep and Glob. A Read of a text file inside a code tree (a .git or .skyrift-workspace marker above it, not under ~/.claude, not a pdf/image/notebook or a pages request), a Grep in files_with_matches or content mode under one (not count mode, a file type filter, multiline, or a pattern JavaScript cannot compile when context lines must be told apart) and a Glob under one are first put to $.tool.check (anything but allow is core's), then answered from the skyline daemon over $.http.fetch (MCP streamable HTTP, one initialize per session, re-initialised once after a daemon restart, marked down for 5 s after a transport failure): skyline's read (full:true, max_match_chars:0) becomes { type, file: { filePath, content, numLines, startLine, totalLines } } with the ¶path#TAG anchor as one context line; skyline's grep (strict:true, max_match_chars:0, limit from head_limit) becomes { mode, filenames, numFiles, totalFiles } or { mode, content, filenames: [], numFiles, numLines, totalLines } with content rendered as ripgrep prints it (cwd-relative paths, path:N:line for a match and path-N-line for context, -- between groups, no path for a single-file search); skyline's find (sort:mtime, limit 100, files only) becomes { filenames, numFiles, totalMatches, truncated, countIsComplete, durationMs } with the rows turned round to core's oldest-first order. Core renders the model-facing text from the record, so core's tool and the classic enforce hook beneath never run. Anything else, and any failure, goes on to core via next(e). Every result's shape is still recorded (stage 1): keys and types, text length, never contents; each new shape announced once in the transcript, every record to the debug log, optionally a JSON shape file.
